lessons.prompt:

Title "GROUP PRECEDENCE: LOWER NUMBER WINS". Premise "A user can belong to multiple groups; one preferred IAM role can be declared in the ID token." Small module label "AWS SECURITY • COGNITO GROUPS", sequence 08. Content: worked example Alice belongs to Readers (precedence 10, ReaderRole) and Editors (precedence 0, EditorRole). Show both group cards feeding a compact priority selector within Cognito USER POOL, selecting EditorRole, output ID token with exact text "cognito:preferred_role → EditorRole" (role names are illustrative, not ARN syntax). Then a separate clear arrow token to "Cognito identity pool" to "Temporary EditorRole credentials". Emphasize user pool puts role information in token; ID token is not AWS credentials. Lower useful group membership illustration: "cognito:groups: Readers, Editors" and "Both memberships remain; precedence selects the preferred role." Separate small note "IAM policies on the selected role determine AWS API permissions." Another small note "Groups cannot be nested." No permissions-union claim, no claim all roles are applied. Avoid code/JSON. Crisp readable exact English, polished integrated modest objects, content-rich but not crowded.

lessons.title: Cognito Sync is legacy data synchronization, not sign-in
lessons.body: Title "COGNITO SYNC: LEGACY DATA, NEW CHOICES". Premise "Data synchronization is separate from signing users in or issuing AWS credentials." Upper left compact old device pair linked through "Cognito Sync — existing implementations" with app preferences, game state and local offline cache. Status exact "Closed to new customers; existing customers can continue." Do not say service shut down. Right content-driven decision fork "New application requirements": "Real-time shared data → AWS AppSync / GraphQL APIs"; "Profiles, preferences, settings → DynamoDB / key-value storage". Do not imply AppSync auto sync offline without client code. Lower migration path old datasets → "Transform data/schema" → "Migrate records" → "Update client APIs + test access controls" → selected new backend. Distinct concise identity note "User pool: sign-in tokens • Identity pool: temporary AWS credentials". AppSync, DynamoDB clear named service nodes and meaningful document, database, device pictograms. No unsupported quotas, no real-time claim for plain DynamoDB. No exact date needed. Balanced two-way comparison, no generic three-card template.

lessons.title: SAML API access returns credentials to the requesting client
lessons.layout: client-centered SAML authentication and STS exchange
lessons.body: Title "SAML API ACCESS: ASSERTION TO SESSION". Premise "The identity provider authenticates the user; AWS STS exchanges the assertion for scoped temporary credentials." Use precise sequence with 4 actors: "Client app", "Corporate IdP", "AWS STS", "Amazon S3". Corporate directory is attached inside IdP side only. First client→IdP "Authenticate"; IdP→client "SAML assertion". Then client→STS "AssumeRoleWithSAML" with small input labels "SAML assertion • RoleArn • PrincipalArn". STS→same client "Access key ID • Secret access key • Session token". Client→S3 "Signed AWS API request"; S3→client "Response". Place trust check near STS "Trusted SAML provider + role trust conditions". Separate role permission document near S3 "Role permissions scope actions and resources". Keep arrows to actual requesters, no direct IdP→S3 route or credential response sent to IdP. No fake AWS logo; company workplace can be modest illustration. Distinguish SAML assertion from AWS credentials with separate colors. Short note "No IAM user is needed for each employee." No runnable code or fabricated console UI.

lessons.title: SAML console federation uses the AWS sign-in endpoint
lessons.layout: browser sequence with sign-in service exchange inset
lessons.body: Title "SAML CONSOLE ACCESS: THE SIGN-IN HANDOFF". Premise "For console SSO, the browser posts the SAML response to AWS Sign-In, which creates the console session." Main actors browser (left), corporate IdP (upper middle), AWS Sign-In (right), AWS Management Console (lower right), AWS STS (small attached exchange near AWS Sign-In). Browser→IdP "Open portal and authenticate"; IdP→browser "SAML response"; browser→AWS Sign-In "POST SAML response"; AWS Sign-In→STS "AssumeRoleWithSAML"; STS→AWS Sign-In "Temporary credentials"; AWS Sign-In→browser "Console redirect"; browser→AWS Management Console "Open federated console session". Make crisp routing avoid crossing unreadable arrows. Lower explanatory notes "The browser does not call AssumeRoleWithSAML directly in this console flow." "Role trust checks the SAML provider and intended audience." "Use configured Regional SAML endpoints for resilient federation." Short contrast "API client flow: call STS directly. Console flow: use AWS Sign-In." No credentials shown as browser local-storage object. No claim console sign-in bypasses role permissions. No console screenshot as this is mechanism not walkthrough.

lessons.title: SAML metadata establishes trust; assertions carry each login
lessons.layout: configuration/runtime distinction with issuer signing-key example
lessons.body: Title "SAML TRUST: METADATA IS NOT A LOGIN". Premise "Configure provider trust once; validate signed assertions for individual sessions." Two related zones with clean fine separator. Configuration upper: Corporate IdP exports "IdP metadata" document with "Issuer identity • Signing certificate / public key" → upload to "IAM SAML provider" → role trust names "Federated SAML provider". Opposite slim arrow AWS service-provider metadata → Corporate IdP labelled "Configure relying party / audience". Do not imply uploading private signing key in ordinary metadata setup. Runtime lower: "User signs in" → IdP issues "Signed SAML assertion" → "AWS validates signature + assertion conditions" → "Role session if authorized". Attached conditions "Intended audience • Assertion time validity • Role attributes". Explicit note "Metadata supplies verification information; it does not itself authenticate the user." Operational note "Monitor signing-key rotation and update provider metadata." Do not say metadata/certificate expiration automatically blocks IAM federation: assertion validity is a distinct check. Make configuration versus runtime visually evident, modest document/certificate/lock pictograms. No exact XML, no unverified signature algorithms.

lessons.title: Direct OIDC federation exchanges a trusted JWT for AWS credentials
lessons.layout: direct workload OIDC path and app identity decision
lessons.body: Title "OIDC FEDERATION: TRUSTED TOKEN, SHORT SESSION". Premise "A trusted OIDC token can be exchanged directly with AWS STS for a scoped role session." Use contemporary worked example CI job (workload pictogram) obtains OIDC token from "OIDC provider" then CI job→AWS STS "AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity" with token and target role, STS→same CI job temporary AWS credentials, CI job→S3 "Signed request". Provider inside separate external identity boundary, STS/S3 are separate services not inside workload/VPC. Beside STS trust gate list "Trusted issuer/provider", "Expected audience (aud)", "Allowed subject (sub)" and "Required provider-specific controls". Explain "Role permissions define the AWS actions allowed." Example compact subject text "Approved repository + branch" no runnable IAM policy. Lower decision note "Direct OIDC suits workload federation. For customer apps needing sign-up, sign-in and identity brokering, consider Amazon Cognito." Highlight "No long-lived AWS keys in the job." Do NOT repeat old blanket claim that direct OIDC is unsupported or universally not recommended. No GitHub logo unless accurate; label CI job generic. No IAM Identity Center conflation.
